drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's ruling about the wife redundant?
outcomeNote: Necessary where other land was designated for her sustenance.

segments.he: וְלֹא לְאִשָּׁה בְּנִכְסֵי בַעְלָהּ וְכוּ׳. פְּשִׁיטָא – כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לַהּ מְזוֹנֵי, מְזוֹנֵי הוּא דְּקָא אָכְלָה! לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּיַחֵד לַהּ אַרְעָא אַחֲרִיתִי לִמְזוֹנַהּ.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And a wife does not have» the ability to establish the presumption of ownership «with regard to her husband’s property.» The Gemara asks: Isn’t that «obvious? Since she has» the right to «sustenance» from her husband’s property, «she is enjoying» the profits as payment of her «sustenance,» so her use of the property does not establish the presumption of ownership. The Gemara responds: «No,» it is «necessary» to state this halakha in the event «that he designated another» parcel of «land for her sustenance.» The mishna teaches that even if she enjoys the profits of a second field for three years, she does not establish the presumption of ownership of that field.
